# Benchmark Radar

> Benchmark Radar tracks new AI benchmarks and evaluations every day, records
> which ones frontier labs actually report in their model cards, and publishes
> the whole collection as an open, evidence-linked dataset anyone can download.

Every claim on the site links back to the document it came from. Scores are
kept partitioned by the source that reported them and are never merged into a
single cross-source ranking, because the sources measure different things and
say so. Where a value is missing, the site says it is missing rather than
showing a zero.

The interactive dashboard has four views. Each heavy view also has a static,
server-delivered summary in the same visual language. The benchmark directory
and evidence blog are plain pages that need no JavaScript to read.

## Start here

- [Benchmark Radar home](https://benchmark-radar.org/): today's newly collected benchmarks, evaluations, and datasets, with the evidence behind each one.
- [Benchmark directory](https://benchmark-radar.org/benchmarks/): every benchmark in the catalog, each with its own page covering what it tests, who published it, and which scores are on record.
- [Model card adoption leaderboard](https://benchmark-radar.org/leaderboard/): which benchmarks frontier labs report in their own model and system cards, plus reported scores over time.
- [Discovery trends](https://benchmark-radar.org/trends/): how many new benchmarks arrive by category, source, and day.
- [Explore the connections](https://benchmark-radar.org/explore/): how benchmarks, datasets, organizations, and sources link to each other.
- [Evidence blog](https://benchmark-radar.org/blog/): daily, source-linked benchmark briefs and reviewed human analysis.
- [Blog archive](https://benchmark-radar.org/blog/archive/): every published daily brief and analysis post.

## Data

- [radar.json](https://benchmark-radar.org/data/radar.json): the complete daily corpus, including every collected record and its evidence. Large file.
- [benchmark-index.json](https://benchmark-radar.org/data/benchmark-index.json): one compact row per benchmark, for search and lookup.
- [models.json](https://benchmark-radar.org/data/models.json): one record per model seen in the curated cards and the crawled score tables.
- [leaderboard.json](https://benchmark-radar.org/data/leaderboard.json): the model card adoption ranking as standalone data. Also published as [leaderboard.csv](https://benchmark-radar.org/data/leaderboard.csv) and [leaderboard.md](https://benchmark-radar.org/data/leaderboard.md).
- [records-badge.json](https://benchmark-radar.org/data/records-badge.json): the current number of collected records.
- [RSS feed](https://benchmark-radar.org/feed.xml): daily evidence briefs and published human analysis.
- [sitemap.xml](https://benchmark-radar.org/sitemap.xml): every indexable page on the site.

Per-benchmark data is served one file per benchmark under
`https://benchmark-radar.org/data/benchmarks/<slug>.json`, where `<slug>` is the
same slug used in that benchmark's page URL.

## Command line

- [Source repository](https://github.com/ktwu01/benchmark-radar): MIT licensed, includes the collection pipeline, the scoring rubric, and the committed daily snapshots the site is built from.
- [Install the CLI](https://github.com/ktwu01/benchmark-radar#query-it-locally-cli-version): `python -m pip install 'git+https://github.com/ktwu01/benchmark-radar.git'`, then `benchmark-radar init` downloads the dataset and `benchmark-radar search` queries it offline.
- [CLI data release](https://github.com/ktwu01/benchmark-radar/releases/tag/cli-data): one checksummed archive of the same data, refreshed on every deploy.

## Optional

- [How the evidence is scored](https://benchmark-radar.org/#rubric): the rubric that decides what gets collected and how strong the evidence behind a record is.
- [Report a problem or suggest a source](https://github.com/ktwu01/benchmark-radar/issues): corrections are welcome, especially wrong attributions.
